messages.subject: selectInput for (Hierarchical, Nested, Tree) data
parts:
This question is somewhat related to the password question in this thread:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/BerC7XCeRD0/TnNaZlvPKt4J

I would like to use Shiny to allow the user to connect to an external data-source.

This data-source may provide a hierarchical list from which the user may wish to make a selection.

I would imagine that such an input could be expressed in R using nested lists, i.e.:

nested_list <- list(
  Canada = list(
    Edmonton = "e123",
    Calgary = "c456"
  ),
  USA = list(
    Seattle = "s789",
    Boston = "b012"
  )
)

In essence, it would be a more-complicated version of selectInput().

Is there, or could there be a way to do this?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.subject: Re: selectInput for (Hierarchical, Nested, Tree) data
parts:
I am working with nested lists as well.
You can make a regular selectInput for each level in the list (two for your example).

After user picks a country in the first selectInput, the second is updated with cities from this country. So no need for an extra component

This sounds obvious, sorry if I got your question wrong.

messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Re: selectInput for (Hierarchical, Nested, Tree) data
parts:
If you know the maximum number of levels your list can have (say n), you can create n controls with renderUI and check if the deeper level is list or not. Something like this
ui.R
....
  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("sel1"),
    uiOutput("sel2"),
    uiOutput("sel3")
  ),

server.R
library(shiny)
# list with inconsistent number of levels (max 3)
data = list(a = "a", b = list(ba = "ba", bb = "bb"), c = list(ca ="ca", cb = list(cba = "cba", cbb = "cbb")))
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    output$sel1 = renderUI(selectInput("sel1", "first", choices=names(data)))
   
    output$sel2 = renderUI({if (is.list(data[[input$sel1]]))
                               selectInput("sel2", "second", choices = names(data[[input$sel1]]))
    })
    output$sel3 = renderUI({if (!is.null(input$sel1) &&
                                !is.null(input$sel2) &&
                                is.list(data[[input$sel1]] [[input$sel2]]))
                                selectInput("sel2", "third", choices = data[[input$sel1]][[input$sel2]])
    })
})

Ugly, but I don't see any better solution. Also, when you don't know the maximum number of levels, it gets tricky: I don't think any recursion is possible inside renderUI.
It's an interesting question.
